FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE June 4, 2026 A Political Transformation in Idaho: Achilles Support Surges in June Poll Significant gains for pragmatic legislators, dissatisfaction with current leadership, and desire for independent leadership dominate the findings in new poll BOISE, Idaho — A growing wave of economic concern, rejection of divisive politicians, and dissatisfaction with the political status quo, is reshaping voter sentiment across Idaho, according to a new statewide survey conducted by the nonpartisan Bullfinch Group. The findings suggest that affordability, government accountability, and nonpartisan problem-solving are emerging as defining issues ahead of the 2026 election cycle which has Todd Achilles emerging as a serious challenger to 83 year old incumbent, Jim Risch. According to the Idaho Capital Sun, in a July 2025 poll from Change Research¹, 3-term Senator Jim Risch’s approval rating was just 41%. As of June 1, 2026, Risch’s approval has dropped to just 30%, with 39% of Idahoans disapproving of his job performance. Support for independent candidates is rapidly growing among informed voters. In a three-way race, polling among informed respondents found that Todd Achilles received 39% support, Senator Jim Risch received 28%, and David Roth received 9%. Idahoans are frustrated with partisan gridlock and losing confidence in the two-party system. According to the Bullfinch survey, 75% of respondents said they want elected officials who are willing to work with both sides of the aisle, reflecting a broad desire for practical solutions over partisan conflict. Idaho’s May 19 closed Republican party primary results reflected this trend. Republican legislators with a track record of pragmatism and bipartisanship beat dogmatic ideologues. Idaho's so-called “Gang of 8” of far-right legislators became a “gang” of three after a rout at the ballot box, with one key race being decided by double digits. The survey also found that 47% of Idaho voters identify the ability to afford everyday essentials, including groceries, gas, and household utilities, as the single most important issue facing families today. The results indicate that concerns about rising costs continue to outweigh national political debates in voters’ minds. "People don't want far right Republicans or far left Democrats… They want hardworking leaders who are there to solve problems, and be a voice for Idahoans " said Todd Achilles. The poll found 62% of respondents identified as independent or “Not Strong Republican” or “Not Strong Democrat.” Todd continued, "There is a growing rejection of the two-party system. In Congress, it doesn't seem to matter which party is in power, we see rising debt, division, and dysfunction. I mean, can anyone really tell the difference between corporatist Republicans and corporatist Democrats?”

The survey also found that 47% of respondents view Senator Jim Risch, 83, as more of a partisan voice for President Donald Trump than an independent voice for Idaho. Respondents additionally expressed concerns about whether elderly elected officials can effectively address rapidly evolving issues such as emerging technologies and artificial intelligence. The findings suggest that Senator Risch's focus on issues such as border security and national security do not align with the immediate concerns of Idaho households. As one of the wealthiest members of the U.S. Senate, Risch has faced increasing scrutiny from voters who say affordability and economic security should receive greater attention. ¹https://idahocapitalsun.com/2025/07/24/new-poll-find-96-idaho-voters-say-public-lands-should-remain-in -public-hands/ ABOUT TODD ACHILLES Todd Achilles, 58, is an Army veteran, former state legislator, public policy professor, and business executive. He grew up on a family farm, served as a U.S. Army tank commander and armor officer, spent over 20 years in senior leadership roles at T-Mobile, Hewlett-Packard, and several technology startups, and served in the Idaho House of Representatives before resigning in July 2025 to launch his U.S. Senate campaign. He lives in Boise with his family. Achilles has spent the past 11 months campaigning across Idaho, visiting all 44 counties and participating in more than 130 public events. Supporters say his extensive outreach reflects a commitment to engaging voters directly and putting the state ahead of party politics. More information can be found at https://www.achillesforidaho.com/ . For media inquiries 208-254-0002 info@achillesforidaho.com
